correctness.rationale: For every d>=3 and real t>0 the proof explicitly lists all 2d+1 vertices, computes the unique positive barycentric minimax support certificate on d affinely independent points, proves strict positive squared-distance clearance of every other vertex, and applies the exact variance identity for all alternative centers. A full vertex-type pairwise-distance classification proves diameter and all equality cases. A separate standard-library Fraction checker passed 220 rational instances and 110220 exact endpoint/distance comparisons; 15 independent convex-hull enumerations confirmed the vertex set. Finite enumeration corroborates but does not replace the symbolic all-real proof.

originality.rationale: The classical definition and coordinate realization of pentasms (arXiv:1509.08218, Section 4) and the 2026 few-vertex decomposability classification (arXiv:2611.07472, Sections 1-3) are prior work. The inspected statements classify faces, edges and Minkowski summands, not the all-dimensional Euclidean minimum-ball contact and diameter equality classes proved here. Five explicit targeted published-finding corpus queries, general mathematical-record searches, and comparisons against accessible previous geometry claims found no equivalent or stronger metric theorem. This is qualified historical priority, not proof of absolute novelty.
residual_risks: Historical priority remains conditional: an unindexed or differently named formula for Euclidean minimum balls of oblique simplex prisms could imply these metric formulas.
The generic minimum-ball methods paper was accessible here only at abstract level; no claim of full-text exclusion is made.
The family is a special coordinate realization rather than all affine pentasms, and the theorem does not extend to the degenerate t=0 boundary.

value.rationale: The object is a canonical, extremal 2d+1-vertex Minkowski-decomposable polytope highlighted in recent 2026 few-vertex classification. The claim gives a natural complete exact Euclidean metric classification for its entire positive-length parameter family, including strict sphere-contact screening (only d contacts out of 2d+1) and the complete K_{2,d-2} diametral structure for arbitrarily large d. These specific geometric data are not fixed by its earlier face-count theorems and provide a benchmark for sparse Minkowski-sum extremal geometry; no general downstream theorem is asserted.
